name: Current rotation
why: This is what you grow today. It is the baseline the other options are compared with.
evidence: Field is bare from July to October (low vegetation, mock)
Water deficit from March to October (mock)
gaps: Your soil type and organic matter are not known yet
risks_to_review: Wheat after wheat can build up root diseases and weeds

name: Legume break
why: A legume adds nitrogen to the soil and breaks the wheat disease cycle.
evidence: Rain falls mostly from October to March, which suits a winter-spring legume (mock)
benefits: Less nitrogen fertilizer for the next wheat
risks_to_review: Chickpea is sensitive to heat in May and June
Ask a local adviser about Ascochyta blight

name: Cover crop in the bare window
why: Your field is bare for about four months. A cover crop (for example vetch with oats) sown with the first autumn rain protects the soil.
evidence: Field likely bare from July to October (mock)
Heavy rain days appear in October and November (mock)
benefits: More organic matter in the soil
gaps: How much water the cover crop takes from the next crop
risks_to_review: In a dry autumn the cover crop may not establish

name: Water-saving swap
why: Sunflower grows in late spring and summer, when your field has the biggest water deficit. Barley and vetch finish earlier.
evidence: Water deficit is largest from May to August (mock)
Hot days increase from June to August (mock)
benefits: Vetch can be sold or used as forage
risks_to_review: Lower income than sunflower in good years
Barley price changes from year to year
